clue.text: Dodge to overtake another old Detroit car (no longer independent)

parts.note: to overtake another vehicle is to pass the other one, read here as PASS THE

indicators.note: no longer having I, the standard abbreviation for independent, so that letter goes

parts.note: Buick is a long-established make of car from the Detroit maker General Motors

explanation.surface: A Dodge car overtakes an old Buick on a Detroit road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge' looks like the car maker, which fits the Detroit scene, but it is the verb defining the answer. 'no longer independent' takes I out of BUICK.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift responsibility onto someone else is to evade or sidestep it, an idiomatic sense of dodging.

clue.text: Shipping line registered a toxic container carrier

parts.note: P&O is a famous British shipping and ferry company, written P AND O
R is a standard abbreviation for registered, as in a registered trademark

explanation.surface: A ferry company is said to have carried a container of poisonous waste.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is the Peninsular and Oriental shipping company. The definition is a playful description of the woman in Greek myth who opened a jar of evils.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the first woman carried a jar or box holding all the world's evils, which escaped when opened.

clue.text: A cross chap, small-time director Nicolas gets upset over empty gesture

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
T is the standard abbreviation for time in physics

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the surname is read bottom to top

parts.note: Nicolas Roeg was the British film director of Don't Look Now

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters with the inside cleared out

explanation.surface: An angry man, a minor director, is annoyed by an empty gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but refers to the red cross on a white flag. 'upset' reverses ROEG to GEOR; 'empty' leaves GE from gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint gives his name to the red cross on the English flag, so he is the man of that cross.

clue.text: Rubbish English gallery

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless rubbish or junk

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses an English art gallery as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is the group of national art galleries in London, Liverpool and St Ives, named after Henry Tate.

clue.text: Brussels is probing Trotter's Mickey Mouse business

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, abbreviated EU

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Rodney Trotter is Del Boy's younger brother in the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses

explanation.surface: EU officials investigate a market trader's dodgy small-time business.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Fools and Horses is a British sitcom about the market-trading Trotter brothers; 'Mickey Mouse' looks like 'trivial' but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme park near Paris is a company whose star character is the famous cartoon mouse, so it is literally his business.

clue.text: Mogul's territory includes historically trouble province

indicators.note: includes means the run of letters is contained within the words Mogul's territory

explanation.surface: A Mughal emperor's realm takes in a troubled region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Troubles were the decades of conflict in Northern Ireland, which is often called by the name of the old province.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Ireland's four historic provinces, the northern one was the setting for decades of sectarian conflict.

clue.text: Christopher secures pooled funds

parts.note: Kit is a familiar short form of the name Christopher
to secure something with a knot or rope is to tie it

explanation.surface: A man named Christopher obtains money from collective funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared pot of money that a group contributes to, like a whip-round.

clue.text: Diplomatic row rumoured to be something to do with Swiss trade

indicators.note: rumoured means heard by word of mouth, so the phrase is identified by its sound

parts.words: something to do with Swiss trade
parts.note: swapping Switzerland's currency, the franc, is a franc exchange

explanation.surface: A rumoured diplomatic dispute concerns Swiss commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: In diplomatic jargon a candid exchange of views is a polite way of saying the talks were an argument.

clue.text: Tender Ezra's curly ringlet

parts.note: Ezra Pound was the American modernist poet, so Ezra's is Pound's

indicators.note: curly means twisted out of shape, so the letters of ringlet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of the poet Ezra Pound's soft curly lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective (gentle) but is a noun: legal tender, money.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is the accepted money of a country, and Britain's currency is the pound.

clue.text: Call Umunna's people about Asian cash

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the group's initials are read backwards

parts.note: the MP Chuka Umunna was part of The Independent Group, known as TIG, in 2019

explanation.surface: Phone a politician's colleagues about some Asian money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent Group was a short-lived 2019 breakaway party of British MPs; TIG reversed gives GIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringgit is the currency of Malaysia, a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Gentleman returned extravagant starter of opulent rice dish

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title or form of address for a gentleman
OTT is short for over the top, meaning extravagant

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man sends back a lavish opulent starter at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian dish is arborio grains cooked slowly in stock until creamy.

clue.text: A right winger, Sebastian's taken aback by Macron's rejection

indicators.note: taken by means held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is French, and the French for no is non

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the surname is reversed

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is the British Olympic runner and athletics administrator

explanation.surface: A conservative named Sebastian is surprised to be snubbed by the French president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like the idiom for surprised, but the two words do separate jobs: 'aback' reverses and 'taken' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoconservative is a hawkish member of the political right, especially in the US.

clue.text: Tackiness of commercial featuring that bloke clutching Oscar

parts.note: ad is short for an advertisement or commercial

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a film featuring that bloke is one he's in
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An advert starring a man holding an Academy Award is tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackiness' suggests poor taste, but here it is literal stickiness. 'clutching' puts O inside HE'S IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticking to a surface is a physical property, the literal sense of tacky as in sticky glue.

clue.text: Rock/metal freak selling old albums here?

indicators.note: to rock is to shake or jolt, so the letters of the phrase are shaken up

explanation.surface: A heavy metal fan sells his old records here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock/metal' looks like music genres, but 'Rock' is the anagram signal for METAL FREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market of second-hand goods is a typical place where old records are sold, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Zealous believer of Everlasting King taken out and shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taken out means removed from the word everlasting

parts.note: R, from the Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A believer in the eternal King is taken outside and shot, a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from EVERLASTING leaves EVELASTING, whose letters 'shot' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher spreading the gospel with fervour is a zealous believer, and the word also means any ardent advocate.

clue.text: Takes 22 tablets

parts.note: 22 across is American, and US is short for the United States
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so tablets are Es

explanation.surface: Someone takes American pills.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to the answer at 22 across, used here as a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To use a substance, such as a drug, is to take it, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Leaves awkward teenager …

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and ungainly, so the letters of teenager are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clumsy adolescent walks out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (goes away) but is a noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of tea is sold as dried leaves, so a pot of them is literally leaves.

clue.text: It might have layers of cracknel occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A dessert might have layers of crunchy brittle.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracknel is a crisp brittle biscuit or toffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge or wedding confection is often built in tiers with filling between, so it is a thing that may be layered.

clue.text: … to take care of mother (don't mention it)

parts.note: to keep someone is to look after or provide for them
mum is the British word for mother

explanation.surface: An awkward teenager is told to look after their mother, but not to speak of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 16 down; read alone, 'don't mention it' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay silent about a secret is the idiom's meaning, so it is a command not to speak of something.

clue.text: Austerity at work, with a dodgy geezer squeezing European head of finance?

indicators.note: squeezing means pressing in between, so one piece goes inside the other
dodgy means unreliable or shifty, so the letters of a geezer are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shady man muscles in on a European finance chief while budgets are tight.
explanation.walkthrough: A geezer is British slang for a man. 'dodgy' rearranges A GEEZER into AGREEZE, and 'squeezing' puts EF inside it after AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding pay level as a cost-cutting measure is economic belt-tightening applied in the workplace.

clue.text: 17 ingredient non-starters for long-legged people?

indicators.note: non-starters means each word loses its first letter

parts.note: leggy means having long legs
folk means people

explanation.surface: The puzzle asks what to call tall people who cannot start a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is CAKE, so the definition is a cake ingredient. 'non-starters' cuts the first letters, L and F, from both words.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow centre of a hen's egg is commonly beaten into sponge mixture as an ingredient.

clue.text: Russia endlessly struggling to attract international star

indicators.note: to attract means to draw in, so one piece goes inside the other
struggling means in difficulty and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the word Russia is cut

explanation.surface: Russia, in decline, is trying to lure a global celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts Russia to RUSSI, 'struggling' rearranges it to SIRUS, and 'to attract' takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dog Star is the brightest star in the night sky, in the constellation Canis Major.

clue.text: From across the pond, a chap touring Morecambe …

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a chap is a man
Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A visitor travels around the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire resort town, which is what the surface suggests; 'the pond' is the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the pond is a jokey idiom for the other side of the Atlantic, so it means from the United States.

clue.text: … Bay area with British nurse girlfriend

parts.note: EN stands for enrolled nurse
gal is an informal word for a girl or girlfriend

explanation.surface: Following on from Morecambe Bay, a British man visits with his nurse girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 22 across, 'Morecambe … Bay' names a bay in north-west England, but this Bay is the one in the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of South Asia lies on the northern shore of the bay that shares its name.

clue.text: Old Alfie's instrument

parts.note: Alfie Boe is an English tenor, so Alfie's points to his surname

explanation.surface: The old singer Alfie has a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind of the orchestra is a musical instrument, an example of the category.

clue.text: 1000 plus 1, 2001, 100, 1000; it's all a stunt!

parts.note: G for grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
I is the Roman numeral for one
MMI is 2001 in Roman numerals
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
K, for kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A list of numbers is dismissed as a mere publicity trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 1000 gives different letters each time: G for a grand and K for kilo.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicity trick designed to attract attention is a stunt, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Used old-fashioned method to validate new money

definitions.meaning: biting a gold piece was an old way to test it was genuine, so this means bit a coin
a digital cryptocurrency launched in 2009 is a new form of money

explanation.surface: Someone checks fresh banknotes the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer describes the past tense of biting a coin to check its metal was real.
explanation.definitionFit: A decentralised digital currency created in 2009 is a modern kind of money.

clue.text: Fail to get nostalgic for former currency

definitions.meaning: to fall short of a target is to fail
to long for the old German Deutschmark is to ...

explanation.surface: Someone fails because they pine for the old currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling short of a target, like an arrow landing wide, is an idiom for failing.
